newsitem.title: FRANCE: Global Studio bid for SFP has payback for state.
newsitem.headline: Global Studio bid for SFP has payback for state.

text.p: A bid by Global Studios, headed by French businessman Walter Butler, for the state-owned SFP film production company includes a provision for returning a portion of future profits to the government, a source close to the deal told Reuters on Friday.

The source said the "return to good fortune" clause envisaged paying a quarter of future profits up to the year 2000, to offset a 1.2 billion franc state recapitalisation sought by Butler in his bid for Societe Francaise de Production (SFP).
A Global Studios spokesman declined to comment.
Butler has forecast that SFP would return to profit in 1999. SFP is expected to make a loss in 1996 of 240 million francs.
He has bid 50 million francs for SFP, which is being privatised by the French government.
He faces a rival bid from Belgian production company LBO Convoy, which is backed by the French media giant Havas. Butler has enlisted the backing of French utilities giant Cie Generale des Eaux.
